subject: pathology
title: Colorectal polyps and carcinoma: pathways and screening

steps.tx: Most colorectal cancers develop slowly from adenomatous polyps over years. The **adenoma carcinoma sequence** starts with APC loss, and **KRAS and TP53 changes** drive later growth and malignancy. This long dwell time makes polypectomy truly preventive, and villous architecture, large size and high grade dysplasia increase malignant risk considerably.
steps.say: Most colon cancers arise from adenomas through a stepwise genetic sequence slowly. APC loss initiates growth and TP53 loss completes malignant transformation later. Polypectomy is preventive because the precursor lesion is removed before invasion occurs. Villous and large polyps are dangerous because malignant risk is higher.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating the adenoma-carcinoma sequence, showing normal mucosa progressing through adenoma stages to carcinoma, with key genetic mutations (APC, KRAS, TP53) at each step.
vis.caption: Adenoma-carcinoma sequence: genetic changes drive polyp progression

steps.tx: Familial adenomatous polyposis carpets the colon with adenomas from adolescence. Germline **APC mutation** causes hundreds of polyps, and **prophylactic colectomy** prevents inevitable cancer in affected patients. Duodenal tumours and desmoid disease also occur, and attenuated polyposis produces fewer polyps later, whereas MUTYH polyposis is inherited recessively.
steps.say: Germline APC failure causes hundreds of adenomas by adolescence in affected families. Cancer is inevitable without colectomy because malignant transformation occurs in polyps eventually. Duodenal tumours develop and desmoid tumours cause significant morbidity after surgery. Family screening starts early because polyps appear during teenage years.

steps.tx: Lynch syndrome causes cancer through defective DNA mismatch repair mechanisms. **Lynch syndrome** produces microsatellite unstable tumours, and **mismatch repair loss** is demonstrated by tumour testing in suspected families. Few polyps precede cancer but progression is rapid, and endometrial, ovarian, gastric and urinary cancers occur in the same families.
steps.say: Lynch syndrome breaks mismatch repair and microsatellite instability develops in tumours characteristically. Few polyps form because cancer progresses rapidly through repair deficient mucosa directly. Right sided tumours occur with prominent tumour infiltrating lymphocytes in many cases. Endometrial cancer is common because extracolonic tumours affect the same families.

left.title: Adenoma carcinoma pathway
points: APC then KRAS then TP53 over years

steps.tx: Right and left sided colon cancers present in distinctly different ways. Right sided tumours cause **occult bleeding** with iron deficiency anaemia, and left sided tumours cause **obstruction** with altered habit and visible bleeding. Carcinoembryonic antigen monitors recurrence rather than screening, and depth of invasion with nodal spread determines staging and prognosis.
steps.say: Right sided cancers bleed occultly because liquid stool hides blood loss initially. Anaemia develops gradually and a vague mass is felt in some patients. Left sided cancers obstruct because the lumen is narrower and stool is formed. Antigen monitoring detects recurrence because levels rise with tumour burden.

steps.tx: Screening and polypectomy reduce both incidence and mortality from colorectal cancer. **Colonoscopy with polypectomy** removes precursor adenomas, and **Peutz Jeghers polyps** with mucocutaneous pigmentation remind us that not all polyps are adenomas. Serrated lesions form a second pathway, and surveillance intervals depend on polyp number, size and histology.
steps.say: Screening reduces mortality because polyps are removed and early cancers are detected. Stool testing and endoscopy are used with earlier starting in familial risk. Peutz Jeghers hamartomas carry pigmentation and intussusception risk in young patients characteristically. Serrated lesions form another pathway because BRAF driven progression occurs separately.

steps.tx: This endoscopic view shows a stalked adenomatous polyp being removed by snare. The **pedunculated adenoma** is caught by **snare polypectomy** around its stalk, and removing it interrupts progression to carcinoma. This preventive effect is the central reason colonoscopic screening reduces both cancer incidence and cancer mortality.
steps.say: This view shows a lobulated polyp on a long stalk inside colon. A snare is looped around the stalk before excision is performed endoscopically. Removal is preventive because adenomas progress to carcinoma over years slowly. Screening reduces mortality because precursor lesions are interrupted early.
